A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SHASTA-PCA research despite the revised title. Text, equations, algorithms, figures, and references support a reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments on subspace estimation, changing subspaces and noise variances, computational timing, and analysis of SDSS quasar spectra.

after.justification: v2 retains these original synthetic experiments and quasar-data analyses in Section 7.

M1.justification: The Gaussian factor model, batch EM algorithm, alternating SHASTA-PCA updates, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The astronomy experiment's per-sample variance adaptation also appears in both versions.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic static-subspace, dynamic-subspace, changing-noise, and timing scenarios, plus the same SDSS DR16Q data. Additional application areas mentioned in v2 are motivation or related work, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same PETRELS and GROUSE baselines, pooled and group-specific PCA/PETRELS variants, HePPCAT variants, and Section 5 batch method where originally evaluated. Added related-work citations do not introduce tested comparators.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, ranks, observation fractions, initialization, hyperparameters, metrics, and baseline preprocessing remain the same. The ten-pass incomplete-quasar evaluation and single-pass timing experiment are retained; the timing and astronomy sections merely exchange order.

E4.justification: The same missing-entry comparisons, abrupt subspace changes, separate doubling of each group's noise variance, and astronomy case study remain. No new ablation, sensitivity experiment, or robustness analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard-deviation ribbons over 50 initializations for Figure 1, 50 randomized repetitions for the fully observed quasar experiment, and one timing run. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run practice changes.

E6.justification: All six figures retain the same underlying results. v1 Figures 4, 5, and 6 become v2 Figures 5, 6, and 4. Reported rankings and findings, including roughly 60% of the batch method's time and 0.0048% of its memory, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical model, EM derivations, updates, and complexity expressions are substantively unchanged. Equations 2–3 re-express the likelihood with an explicit parameter-independent constant. v1's convergence discussion and Equation 42 move to v2 Section 6.3.1 and Equation 38; no proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal claims about joint streaming estimation, missing entries, heteroscedastic noise, efficiency, and improved subspace tracking remain. v2 foregrounds the alternating-surrogate and learned-regularization connections already discussed in v1 Sections 6.4 and 8.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explanation that separate approximate minorizers reduce memory and computational overhead relative to a joint surrogate. Section 6.4 newly explains that alternative variance minorizers did not appear more efficient. Most convergence limitations are retained through relocation.

D1.justification: Both provide the same algorithm initialization, experiment hyperparameters, quasar selection and preprocessing references, and Julia implementation and hardware disclosure. No code or data-access information is substantively added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of streaming PCA, stochastic MM, and heteroscedastic inference. Additions include Markovian Oja analysis, robust and federated/distributed PCA, nonstationary probabilistic PCA, variance-reduced MM, and heteroscedastic bandits, broadening the research context beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises the introduction, and polishes prose throughout. It moves convergence discussion from the conclusion into Section 6.3.1 and swaps the timing and astronomy subsections. The overall exposition and most technical text remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title/author layout, headings, and spacing. Figure 1 changes from four horizontally arranged plots to two stacked pairs with separate legends; other plots are substantially enlarged, and timing and astronomy figures are relocated. The plotted evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability through larger, better-arranged figures and places convergence caveats beside the algorithm. Expanded related work provides more current context. These support a limited overall quality gain, while the method, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
